text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: dedicated-resv pool 'resv-prod-eu-west-1' >= 96% GPU utilization. Queue length spiked for reserved tenants, autoscaler attempts failing. Root cause unknown.

mike-oncall: I'm on it — pinging infra (+raj) and SRE. Any immediate customer 5xxs?

sabrina-plateng: @mike-oncall metrics show enqueue growth on reserved queue for tenant CobaltAnalytics and some preemptible jobs still running on the pool. Latency SLOs for dedicated routes are spiking.

raj-ml: looks like a small burst from CobaltAnalytics long-context workloads. However autoscaler is hitting rate-limits in the control plane: "scale_up_quota_exceeded" in recent logs.

jess-infra: verifying autoscaler logs now. Also seeing frequent failed scale attempts: api 429 from resourcemanager. Could be quota or rate-limit policy in the control plane that prevented new nodes from being provisioned.

leo-sre: if autoscaler cannot add capacity fast enough we need to protect reserved tenants. Two live actions: 1) pause lower-priority jobs on this pool; 2) route enterprise reserved traffic to fallback variant in another region (if allowed).

mike-oncall: runbook step A: identify non-reserved allocations on pool and evict. @jess-infra can you run the eviction command?

jess-infra: running eviction dry-run then exec. Command:```sh
# list non-reserved allocations
rictl nodes list --pool resv-prod-eu-west-1 --format json | jq '.allocations[] | select(.reservation==null)'
# evict non-reserved
rictl allocation evict --pool resv-prod-eu-west-1 --filter reservation==null --reason "incident: protect reserved tenants"
```

ops-runbook-bot: Reminder — evicting allocations will restart running jobs. Confirm before executing.

mike-oncall: confirmed, proceed. @taylor-csm please notify CobaltAnalytics about potential short restarts for some non-reserved workloads (they may see infer latency improve).

taylor-csm: on it, pinging account team and CS lead. Notifying CobaltAnalytics: "we're actively mitigating a capacity issue affecting reserved latency; non-critical jobs will be evicted to restore service". Will share ETA once we know.

raj-ml: autoscaler log snippet: ```{"ts":"...","err":"scale_up_quota_exceeded","attempts":4,"pool":"resv-prod-eu-west-1"}``` Looks like an API rate quota from cloud provider or internal limit.

jess-infra: cloud console shows VM quota still available but our internal request queue hit a throttling window. Opening internal rate-limit ticket to infra control plane. Temp workaround: spawn a small manual allocation from a different capacity class and attach to pool.

leo-sre: manual allocation strategy accepted — create 2x p4d-similar instances in eu-west-1 and attach as dedicated nodes to the pool. That should buy time. @jess-infra can you provision? Use tag "incident-temp-surge".

jess-infra: provisioning now, ETA ~6 minutes. Command:```sh
cloudctl compute create --type p4d --count 2 --region eu-west-1 --tags incident-temp-surge
cloudctl attach --pool resv-prod-eu-west-1 --instances $(last-created-ids)
```

mike-oncall: good. Meanwhile, throttling measures — reduce per-tenant concurrency for non-enterprise routes to free slots. Update route config: set concurrency_limit=1 for /generate on non-reserved. @sabrina-plateng can you push this change?

sabrina-plateng: pushing a temporary ACL:```yaml
routes:
  - name: public-generate
    concurrency_limit: 1
    priority: best-effort
``` Pushing now.

ops-runbook-bot: note — changing concurrency limits may increase latencies for lower tiers. Proceed?

mike-oncall: proceed. Priority is protecting reserved tenants.

(6 minutes later) jess-infra: manual nodes are up and attached. Pool capacity increased by 2 GPUs. Utilization dropped to 87%. Queue drain started.

leo-sre: great. Monitor for noisy neighbor — there were signs of a single CobaltAnalytics job holding multiple GPUs due to very long sequence lengths. If it keeps grabbing most slots we may need to throttle that tenant specifically.

raj-ml: inspected job IDs: `cobalt-long-ctx-9921` is still running and consuming 8/12 GPUs on one node. Could be misconfigured batch size/seq-length. Recommend reducing max_gpu_per_job for tenant to 4 as short-term.

mike-oncall: @jess-infra can we enforce a tenant cap? Runbook allows throttle: `rictl tenant update --id cobaltanalytics --max-gpus 4 --reason "incident mitigation"`

jess-infra: applying tenant cap now.

ops-runbook-bot: automated alert — tenant cap applied. Monitor for regression.

taylor-csm: CobaltAnalytics acknowledged the note. They're investigating long-ctx job. CS will coordinate to avoid surprise restarts for their critical jobs.

mike-oncall: summary/actions: 1) evicted non-reserved jobs from pool (done); 2) applied temp concurrency limits on public routes (done); 3) provisioned 2 manual nodes (done); 4) applied tenant cap on cobaltanalytics (done); 5) opened control-plane rate-limit ticket (jess & infra).

leo-sre: next steps: 1) follow-up with control plane to lift throttle window / adjust backoff config; 2) plan longer-term: increase reserved pool headroom for enterprise tiers or add fast-path pre-warm instances; 3) schedule post-incident with ML infra + product to discuss model/job misconfigs.

mike-oncall: I'll run postmortem template — tagging for severity P2 due to degraded latency for reserved customers and customer-visible restarts for non-reserved. Assigning owners: jess for infra, raj for workload mitigations, taylor for customer comms.

jess-infra: created infra ticket INC-9876 linking autoscaler traces and cloud api 429s.

raj-ml: will run job cost/profile analysis for cobalt-long-ctx-9921 and propose model/seq size limits.

taylor-csm: shared interim status with CobaltAnalytics and set expectation for a detailed follow-up.

mike-oncall: closing incident channel when metrics stable for 30m and no regressions. For now keep thread live. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
